en: The Glorification of the Holy Gaṅgā (Śrīgaṅgāstotra)

O Goddess, Sovereign of the Gods, Blessed Gaṅgā, who delivers the three worlds with your most shimmering waves, O stainless one who sport upon the crest of Śaṅkara—may my mind rest within your lotus feet. 1.
O Mother, bestower of happiness upon Bhagīratha, the greatness of your waters is celebrated in the Vedas; yet I do not know your true majesty—protect me, O compassionate one, from my ignorance.

O Gaṅgā, river of the lotus feet of Hari, with waves as white as snow, the moon, and pearls; remove the burden of my misdeeds and, by your grace, lead me to the further shore of the ocean of worldly existence. || 3 ||
He who has drunk your pure water has indeed attained the supreme state; O Mother Gaṅgā, Yama is truly powerless even to look upon one who is devoted to you.

O Jāhnavī Gaṅgā, who uplifts the fallen; O you whose breaking of the mountain-king's pride was magnificent; O mother of Bhīṣma, O daughter of the best of sages; O you who ward off those who have fallen, O you who are the glory of the three worlds! || 5 ||

O Gaṅgā, who sport on both banks of the ocean and cast tremulous side-glances from the faces of young women, he who bows to you—who, like a wish-fulfilling creeper, bestows fruit in this world—does not fall into sorrow.
O Mother Gaṅgā, Jāhnavī, who wards off hell, who destroys impurity, and whose greatness is sublime—even he who has bathed in your stream is not born again in a womb.

Again, O Jāhnavī, whose waves are more meritorious than the other [rivers], victory, victory to you, O goddess with compassionate glances! Your feet are adorned by the jewels in Indra’s crown; O giver of happiness, giver of auspiciousness, refuge of your servants! || 8 ||

O Blessed One, remove my disease, grief, torment, and sin, as well as the mass of my evil thoughts; O you who are the essence of the three worlds and the sustainer of the earth, you are indeed my refuge in this cycle of existence.
O Alakānandā, supreme bliss, O you who are full of compassion and worthy of the devotion of the distressed! For one whose dwelling is near your banks, their residence is indeed in Vaikuṇṭha. (10)

Better here in the water is a tortoise or a fish, or perhaps on the shore a withered lizard; or else a filthy and wretched outcaste—certainly not one born of a royal lineage who is not far from you. (11)

O Bhuvaneśvarī, O meritorious and blessed Goddess, O daughter of the excellent sage who consists of flowing water! That man who constantly recites this stainless hymn of praise to Gaṅgā truly triumphs. (12)
In the hearts of those who possess devotion to Gaṅgā, there is always happiness and liberation, rendered charming by the sweet, beloved, and most blissful songs of the Pañjhaṭikas. || 13 ||

This hymn to the Gaṅgā, which is the essence of existence, bestows desired fruits, and is pure and quintessential—composed by Śaṅkara for the service of Śaṅkara—is recited by those who are happy; thus it is concluded. 14.
